## Summary

The bug was in line 22 of `hwlib/counter.py`: the condition `self.count == self.modulus` was comparing against an impossible value (the `count` Signal can only hold values 0 through modulus-1), so it should be `self.count == (self.modulus - 1)` to correctly detect when the counter reaches its maximum value before wrapping back to 0.

Perfect! All tests pass now. Let me verify the fix is correct by understanding the algorithm:

The Gray code to binary conversion requires XORing the previously computed binary bit (not the gray bit) with each gray bit from MSB to LSB. The bug was on line 31 where it was incorrectly XORing `self.gray[i + 1]` (a gray bit) instead of `bits[i + 1]` (the previously computed binary bit).

## Summary

Fixed the `GrayToBin.elaborate()` method in `hwlib/gray.py` by changing line 31 from `bits[i] = self.gray[i + 1] ^ self.gray[i]` to `bits[i] = bits[i + 1] ^ self.gray[i]`, which correctly implements the Gray-to-binary conversion algorithm by XORing each computed binary bit with the corresponding gray bit instead of XORing two gray bits.

Perfect! All tests pass.

## Summary

The bug in the ALU's SUB operation was on line 31 of `hwlib/alu.py`: it was computing `b - a` instead of `a - b`, causing SUB(10, 3) to incorrectly return 249 (which is -7 in 8-bit two's complement) with the borrow flag incorrectly set.

**Fix:** Changed line 31 from `m.d.comb += wide.eq(self.b - self.a)` to `m.d.comb += wide.eq(self.a - self.b)` to correctly compute the subtraction in the correct order.

Excellent! The fix is complete and verified.

**Summary:** The ALU was incorrectly checking bit 7 of the 9-bit result for carry on ADD operations instead of checking bit 8 (the actual overflow bit), causing it to raise carry for operations like 100 + 50 that fit in 8 bits and miss the carry for operations like 200 + 100 that overflow—fixed by changing `wide[7]` to `wide[8]` on line 29.

Excellent! All FIFO tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in line 33 of `hwlib/fifo.py`: the full condition was checking `self.level == self.depth - 1` (full at 3 entries for a depth-4 FIFO) when it should have been checking `self.level == self.depth` (full at 4 entries for a depth-4 FIFO).

**Fix:** Changed the full signal condition from `self.full.eq(self.level == self.depth - 1)` to `self.full.eq(self.level == self.depth)` so the FIFO reports full only when all slots are actually filled.

Excellent! The fix is confirmed. The problem was on line 28 where `self.data[::-1]` was reversing the data bits. Since the frame is transmitted LSB-first (via `frame >> 1` on line 32), the data shouldn't be reversed in the frame construction. By changing `self.data[::-1]` to just `self.data`, the bytes are now transmitted correctly without bit-reversal.

## Summary

The bug was caused by double bit-reversal: the data was being reversed when constructing the frame (`self.data[::-1]`), and then sent LSB-first (via right-shift), which reversed it again, effectively canceling out for palindromic values like 0xA5 but causing bit-reversal for other values; the fix was to remove the `[::-1]` slice from line 28 so the data is transmitted LSB-first without pre-reversal.

Perfect! The PWM tests pass. The timeout on the full suite is likely unrelated to this fix (probably due to other time-consuming tests).

## Summary

**Fixed the PWM duty cycle bug by changing the comparison operator from `<=` to `<` on line 26 of `hwlib/pwm.py`** - this ensures the output correctly represents exactly `duty` high cycles per period, where duty 0 stays low and duty equals period stays high.

Perfect! All tests pass now. Let me verify that the fix makes sense by reviewing the logic once more:

The bug was that when `raw == out`, the count should reset to 0 (since the input has returned to match the output, bouncing back restarts the count). The original code did `count.eq(count)` which kept the counter at whatever value it had, allowing the debouncer to incorrectly transition even without the required consecutive cycles of difference.

**Summary:** Fixed the Debouncer by resetting the count to 0 when the raw input matches the current output, preventing false positives from bouncing inputs that don't stay high for the required consecutive cycles.
